Question: Multi-Sensor Navigation for an Autonomous Robot in an Indoor-Outdoor Environment

Scenario:

An autonomous robot is navigating a warehouse where GPS signals are weak indoors but strong outdoors. The robot must use a Hybrid Navigation System combining:

  1. GPS (Works outdoors but unreliable inside)
  2. INS (Inertial Navigation System) (Provides position changes but drifts over time)
  3. Wi-Fi Positioning System (WPS) (Used for indoor tracking)

The robot switches between navigation methods based on its environment:

  • If GPS is available, use GPS + INS (GPS corrects INS drift).
  • If GPS is lost, use WPS + INS (WPS corrects INS drift).

Each navigation method has a reliability score:

  • GPS = 0.5 (Can be inaccurate in urban areas)
  • INS = 0.3 (Reliable in short periods but drifts over time)
  • WPS = 0.2 (Only works indoors)

The final corrected position is computed using sensor fusion:

Final Position=(w1​×Primary Sensor)+(w2​×INS)

where weights w1 and w2 depend on the available navigation method.

Task:

Write a Python program that:

  1. Inputs:
    • Initial GPS position (latitude, longitude)
    • INS displacement (meters moved in x and y)
    • WPS estimated position (latitude, longitude)
    • Environment Type ("Indoor" or "Outdoor")
  2. Computes the robot's final corrected position using:
    • GPS + INS if outdoor
    • WPS + INS if indoor
  3. Outputs:
    • The corrected position based on the navigation method used.

Hints:

  • Convert INS displacement into latitude/longitude shifts using:

1 meter≈0.00001 degrees latitude/longitude

  • Adjust weights w1 and w2 based on the available sensors.
  • Use weighted averaging to integrate multiple data sources.
